root_cause.text: `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback()` in the `ems_usb` CAN USB driver parsed a variable-length message stream using `urb->transfer_buffer_length` instead of `urb->actual_length`, and it also failed to verify that enough bytes remained before dereferencing each `struct ems_cpc_msg`, enabling out-of-bounds reads when USB payloads were shorter than expected.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a pre-check `if (start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN > urb->actual_length)` before casting `&ibuf[start]` to `struct ems_cpc_msg`, and changes the end-of-message bound check from `start > urb->transfer_buffer_length` to `start > urb->actual_length`; the commit message explicitly states that `actual_length` is the real received size and that both the beginning and end of parsing must be checked to avoid overflow past the buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent out-of-bounds parsing of malformed USB message data.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added inside the bulk receive loop before casting the buffer at `start` to `struct ems_cpc_msg`: if `start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN > urb->actual_length`, the code logs `netdev_err(netdev, "format error\n")` and breaks out of the loop.
intent_record.how: This prevents the driver from reading past the end of the received USB buffer when processing CPC messages. If the incoming data is truncated or malformed, the callback now detects the invalid message header position and stops parsing instead of dereferencing out-of-bounds memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the bulk receive parser to use the URB's actual received length when detecting malformed message framing.
intent_record.what: In the bulk read callback, the bounds check for the parsing cursor changed from comparing `start` against `urb->transfer_buffer_length` to comparing it against `urb->actual_length`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser now validates consumed message bytes against the amount of data actually received in the URB rather than the size of the allocated transfer buffer, preventing it from treating unread or uninitialized buffer space as valid input.

This is the pre-fix malformed-frame check that used transfer_buffer_length instead of actual_length, allowing the parser to trust an incorrect size and continue parsing beyond the real received data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This check used urb->transfer_buffer_length instead of the URB's actual received length, so the parser could believe more data was available than was actually present and continue parsing a truncated USB payload, leading to out-of-bounds reads.

This dereferences a message header from the receive buffer without first ensuring enough bytes remain for a full struct ems_cpc_msg, which is the unchecked variable-length parse that can read past the end of a short USB transfer.
This accesses a field of the potentially out-of-bounds ems_cpc_msg immediately after the unchecked cast, so if the buffer is shorter than expected the read of msg->type can itself go out of bounds.

commit 702171adeed3607ee9603ec30ce081411e36ae42
Author: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 16 02:04:20 2009 +0000

    ems_usb: Added support for EMS CPC-USB/ARM7 CAN/USB interface
    
    This patch adds support for one channel CAN/USB interace CPC-USB/ARM7 from
    EMS Dr. Thomas Wuensche (http://www.ems-wuensche.com).
    
    Signed-off-by: Sebastian Haas <haas@ems-wuensche.com>
    Signed-off-by: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable receive path is present in `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback()`. The code parses a variable-length message stream with `msg = (struct ems_cpc_msg *)&ibuf[start];` and then immediately dereferences `msg->type` and later `msg->length` without first checking that a full `struct ems_cpc_msg` or even the header is within the received payload. The only length-related guard is after processing: `start += CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN + msg->length; ... if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length) { ... break; }`, which uses `urb->transfer_buffer_length` instead of `urb->actual_length`. This matches the root cause: short USB transfers can cause out-of-bounds reads because the code trusts the buffer allocation length rather than the actual received length. There is no fix here; the callback lacks a pre-dereference bounds check and uses the wrong length field.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable parsing logic is present in this function. In `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback()`, the code parses a variable-length stream using `urb->actual_length` only for the outer check: `if (urb->actual_length > CPC_HEADER_SIZE) { ... }`, but then advances through messages with `start += CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN + msg->length;` and compares against `urb->transfer_buffer_length` instead of the received byte count: `if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length) { ... }`. This matches the root cause of using the buffer's maximum size rather than the actual USB payload length. The function also dereferences `msg->type` and `msg->length` immediately after `msg = (struct ems_cpc_msg *)&ibuf[start];` without first verifying that enough bytes remain for a full `struct ems_cpc_msg` header, so the missing bounds check is also present. There is no fix here: the code does not validate `start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN <= urb->actual_length` or similar before dereferencing each message.
